title: Rivergate and Monsoon
premise: Elodie Galloway, a salvage diver scraping a living from the drowned town of Rivergate, recovers a chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a nation erased from every map forty years ago. The navy that sank it wants the chest and everyone who touched it buried, while a Vessian exile network wants its contents to resurrect a claim to power. Hunted by both and bound by loyalty to her crew, Elodie must decide whether the truth inside the chest is worth the lives it will cost. In the end she scatters the evidence into the monsoon floodwaters, exposing the navy's crime without handing power to the exiles, and chooses a new identity on open water.
about_author: Gideon Vane is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent a decade running salvage contracts along forgotten inland waterways. They write adventure fiction about people who live where governments stop looking.

chapters.title: The Water Keeps Its Dead
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A routine dive on the wreck of the corvette Vessant brings up a sealed chest stamped with the Vessian double-star. Her partner Tamir urges throwing it back; her instinct says it's worth money. The beat is uneasy curiosity curdling into dread when a navy patrol boat appears upstream, unannounced and slow.

chapters.title: Navy Business
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Corvane's POV. Corvane arrives at Rivergate with salvage permits and soft questions, revealing the navy has been quietly dredging this stretch for years. He offers Elodie a finder's fee for 'any artifacts of foreign origin.' The beat is polite menace; Elodie realizes the wreck was never lost, only hidden.

chapters.title: What the Chest Holds
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Cracking the chest in her boathouse, she finds documents proving the Vessant carried exiled officials the navy executed rather than repatriate, plus a ledger naming collaborators still in power. Tamir wants to sell it; deckhand Sefa wants to burn it. The beat is fractured loyalty as the crew splits over what truth demands.

chapters.title: The Exile's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilse Marchetti's POV. A woman claiming to be Vessian nobility finds Elodie through an old smuggler contact, offering protection and wealth if the chest reaches her network across the border. She reveals the navy has already killed one diver who found something similar. The beat is temptation wrapped in fear: safety at the price of becoming someone else's instrument.

chapters.title: Rivergate Locks Down
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Navy checkpoints seal the river; Corvane searches boats and posts a reward for 'stolen government property.' Sefa hides the documents inside the hull ballast and lies to a soldier with steady hands and shaking knees. The beat is terror and unexpected courage as the quietest crew member becomes the load-bearing liar.

chapters.title: Tamir's Price
chapters.summary: Tamir's POV. Desperate for his daughter's medical debt, Tamir secretly photographs the ledger and contacts Corvane, intending to trade a copy for cash and immunity. Halfway through the meeting he sees the reward notice lists three names, not one. The beat is guilt and reversal: he walks out without selling, now knowing betrayal buys nothing but graves.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With the storm days away and Corvane closing in, Elodie plans to run the rapids at night with the chest. Marchetti intercepts her, dropping the noble act and revealing the exiles will kill the crew once they have the documents. The beat is betrayal confirmed and resolve hardened: there is no safe buyer, only a choice about who gets the truth.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Vessant
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Ordered to destroy the wreck and any witnesses, Corvane mines the site but hesitates, having read enough of the file to know his superiors are erasing their own crime. When Marchetti's armed exiles attack the navy camp simultaneously, chaos erupts. The beat is a man discovering his obedience serves corruption, choosing which order to disobey first.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Climax. During the monsoon's first night, Elodie runs the flooded rapids with the chest while exiles and navy fight ashore. Tamir takes a bullet shielding the ballast hatch; Corvane, defecting, covers their escape and goes down with his patrol boat buying them minutes. The beat is sacrifice and fury as Elodie opens the chest above the flood and feeds the documents to the river.

chapters.title: What the River Carries
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Resolution. The papers are gone, but Elodie kept copies of three names and mails them, one by one, from different towns, letting justice move slowly and deniably. Tamir survives; the crew takes new names and a new boat. The beat is bittersweet freedom: the truth is loose in the world, and Elodie finally belongs to no flag but her own.
